jobs.excerpt: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based at our HQ in central Zurich or in Munich.

About the role

You solve the hard technical problems on live systems.

Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right.

That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you.

Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one.

Stabilising accounts
When an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is.

Taking effort out permanently
Anything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly.

You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap.

You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you.

You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging.

What you'll do

  • Own the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause.

  • Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic.

  • Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering.

  • Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly.

  • Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants.

  • Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities.

  • Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once.

  • Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone.

  • Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function.

  • Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations.

What we're really looking for

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why.

  • Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is.

  • Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you.

  • Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving.

  • Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster.

  • Stabilizer Under Pressure: An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silence

What you'll bring

  • Master's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case.

  • 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent.

  • Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs.

  • Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume.

  • German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.

  • Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining.

What you'll get

  • The hard problems, not the queue.

  • Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product.

  • Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built.

  • Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Frontend

Backend

Required Skills

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
jobs.excerpt: About Dynime Dynime is an AI-powered digital transformation company helping businesses build, operate, automate, and scale their digital infrastructure across technology, software, digital services, automation, business infrastructure, and international markets.
jobs.description:
About Dynime

Dynime is an AI-powered digital transformation company helping businesses build, operate, automate, and scale their digital infrastructure across technology, software, digital services, automation, business infrastructure, and international markets.

We are seeking an experienced Chief Executive Officer to lead Dynime's next stage of growth and build a scalable, profitable, technology-driven, internationally competitive organization.

Role Overview

The CEO is responsible for Dynime's overall strategic direction, business performance, growth, profitability, culture, organizational development, and long-term value creation. The successful candidate will lead the executive team, establish company-wide priorities, drive sustainable revenue growth, develop strategic relationships, oversee financial and operational performance, support international expansion, and ensure strong execution of Dynime's business strategy.

Primary Objectives

The CEO will be responsible for:

  • Establishing and executing Dynime's long-term vision and strategy.

  • Driving sustainable revenue and customer growth.

  • Improving profitability and financial sustainability.

  • Expanding Dynime into international markets.

  • Strengthening products, technology, AI, and automation initiatives.

  • Building scalable operational systems and leadership structures.

  • Developing a high-performance executive team and company culture.

  • Building strategic customer, partner, and stakeholder relationships.

  • Protecting the company's reputation, assets, and long-term interests.

Key Responsibilities

Corporate Strategy

  • Define Dynime's long-term corporate strategy and strategic priorities.

  • Establish annual, quarterly, and multi-year objectives.

  • Translate strategy into measurable business plans and KPIs.

  • Evaluate new products, services, markets, and business models.

  • Monitor competitors, market conditions, and growth opportunities.

  • Ensure departments remain aligned with company strategy.

Business Growth & Commercial Leadership

  • Own the overall company growth strategy.

  • Develop new revenue streams and commercial opportunities.

  • Expand the international customer base.

  • Support enterprise sales and strategic negotiations.

  • Build strategic partnerships and business relationships.

  • Work closely with the CCO, VP Sales, and business development leadership.

  • Review sales pipeline, forecasts, pricing, customer acquisition, retention, and expansion.

  • Identify opportunities for strategic investments, acquisitions, or alliances.

Financial Performance

  • Maintain executive ownership of company-level financial performance.

  • Work with the CFO on budgets, forecasts, cash flow, profitability, and financial planning.

  • Monitor revenue, margins, operating expenses, and financial sustainability.

  • Establish company financial targets.

  • Ensure responsible allocation of resources and major expenditures.

  • Make informed decisions using financial and operational data.

Executive Leadership

  • Lead Dynime's executive leadership team.

  • Establish clear responsibilities, priorities, and accountability.

  • Review executive performance and departmental KPIs.

  • Resolve executive-level conflicts and organizational issues.

  • Develop future senior and executive leaders.

  • Promote ownership, accountability, transparency, and execution.

International Expansion

  • Establish international market priorities and expansion strategies.

  • Identify high-potential countries and regions.

  • Evaluate market-entry opportunities.

  • Support regional leadership and international sales teams.

  • Build international strategic partnerships.

  • Monitor international revenue and market performance.

  • Maintain consistent global positioning.

Priority markets may include North America, Europe, United Kingdom, Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and Africa.

Technology, AI & Product

  • Work closely with the CTO on technology strategy and product development.

  • Understand major technology and product initiatives.

  • Evaluate significant technology investments.

  • Support AI, automation, SaaS, and digital transformation initiatives.

  • Ensure technology investments support business objectives.

  • Evaluate product-market fit, scalability, security, and infrastructure requirements.

  • Identify opportunities for AI-enabled products and services.

Operations & Organization

  • Build scalable organizational structures and operating systems.

  • Define departmental responsibilities and management accountability.

  • Review operational performance and remove organizational bottlenecks.

  • Improve decision-making and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Promote automation, efficiency, and process improvement.

  • Ensure company policies and operating standards are followed.

Governance & Risk

  • Maintain professional executive governance and accountability.

  • Support board and ownership reporting.

  • Work with legal, financial, and other professional advisors.

  • Identify and manage major financial, operational, technology, cybersecurity, legal, regulatory, market, reputation, and business continuity risks.

  • Protect Dynime's confidential information, assets, customers, and reputation.

Customers & Stakeholders

  • Develop relationships with strategic customers and partners.

  • Represent Dynime in major negotiations and business meetings.

  • Support high-value enterprise opportunities.

  • Handle critical executive-level customer escalations.

  • Communicate Dynime's strategy and direction to key stakeholders.

People & Culture

  • Establish and reinforce company values and leadership standards.

  • Build a high-performance, professional, and internationally minded culture.

  • Encourage innovation and responsible experimentation.

  • Support employee and leadership development.

  • Promote ethical conduct, accountability, and transparent communication.

  • Lead through clear expectations and measurable outcomes rather than unnecessary micromanagement.

Required Capabilities

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

  • Strategic Leadership: Ability to develop long-term strategy and execute it through measurable objectives.

  • Commercial Judgment: Strong understanding of customers, markets, pricing, sales, partnerships, and revenue.

  • Financial Literacy: Strong understanding of P&L, cash flow, margins, EBITDA, budgets, forecasting, and financial risk.

  • Executive Leadership: Ability to lead senior executives and build organizational accountability.

  • Decision Making: Ability to make timely, evidence-based decisions while managing risk.

  • International Business: Ability to operate across international markets and cultures.

  • Technology Understanding: Executive-level understanding of SaaS, AI, automation, cloud technology, software, cybersecurity, and digital transformation.

  • Communication: Excellent communication with employees, customers, executives, partners, investors, and board-level stakeholders.

  • Negotiation: Strong ability to negotiate strategic partnerships, enterprise contracts, investments, and commercial agreements.

  • Organizational Development: Ability to build scalable teams, processes, structures, and management systems.

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • 10+ years of professional experience.

  • Significant executive, senior management, founder, or general management experience.

  • Experience leading a company, business unit, division, or major organizational function.

  • Demonstrated business growth and commercial leadership experience.

  • Experience managing senior leadership teams.

  • Strong understanding of financial and operational performance.

  • International business exposure.

  • Excellent communication, leadership, and decision-making skills.

Preferred

  • Experience in technology, SaaS, AI, digital services, consulting, automation, or digital transformation.

  • Experience scaling an international business.

  • Founder or entrepreneurial experience.

  • Enterprise sales or commercial leadership experience.

  • Experience with strategic partnerships, investments, or corporate development.

Performance KPIs

The CEO will be evaluated primarily on company-level outcomes, including:

  • Growth: Revenue growth, customer growth, international revenue, enterprise customer growth.

  • Financial: Gross margin, EBITDA/operating profitability, cash flow, budget performance, and financial sustainability.

  • Commercial: New business revenue, customer retention, expansion revenue, strategic partnership revenue.

  • Operations: Operational efficiency, departmental performance, employee productivity, leadership effectiveness.

  • Strategic: Successful market expansion, product development, strategic partnerships, and long-term business value creation.

First 90 Days

  • First 30 Days: Understand the business model, financial position, organizational structure, products, customers, sales pipeline, market position, risks, and immediate priorities.

  • Days 31–60: Establish strategic priorities, review departmental KPIs, identify growth opportunities, strengthen executive accountability, review international expansion, and develop an executive operating plan.

  • Days 61–90: Finalize the strategic roadmap, establish measurable company objectives, implement executive performance reporting, define major growth initiatives, and present a clear 12-month business plan.

Leadership Principles

The CEO is expected to:

  • Think long-term and execute decisively.

  • Prioritize sustainable growth over vanity metrics.

  • Make decisions using data, judgment, and evidence.

  • Maintain accountability at every leadership level.

  • Delegate effectively while maintaining strategic control.

  • Protect customer trust and company reputation.

  • Build scalable systems rather than relying on individuals.

  • Encourage innovation while managing unnecessary risk.

  • Maintain professional and ethical business practices.

  • Maintain consistent international standards.

Compensation & Benefits

Annual Base Salary: USD $100,000–$180,000.

Final compensation depends on experience, leadership capability, international expertise, scope of responsibility, and negotiated employment terms.

Additional compensation may include:

  • Performance bonus

  • Revenue or profitability-based incentives

  • Equity/ownership participation

About Darkroom

Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the role

We are looking for a deeply technical Senior Retention Specialist to own the CRM build for a high-growth consumer technology client. You will architect and implement the flows and automations that carry the program, own the segmentation logic behind them, and hold the channel KPIs that determine whether any of it lands in the inbox.

You are standing this program up from the ground, not inheriting it. The list starts near 20,000 and scales rapidly behind a significant acquisition investment — which puts real pressure on deliverability, list hygiene, and data hygiene from day one. Volume ramps to 40–60 emails a month, and increasingly granular segmentation is what generates that output. Automation is the core of the program: lead capture, welcome series, and the first-conversion funnel first, then subscription activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back. You will work in an enterprise-grade platform — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

You are the person who knows the platform better than anyone else on the team. When something does not fire, does not render, or does not deliver, you find out why.

You should apply if this sounds like you

You are hands-on in the ESP every day and you like it there. You enjoy building a journey with real conditional logic, and you get genuine satisfaction from tracking down why one segment stopped converting.

  • 3–5+ years of hands-on lifecycle, CRM, or email marketing execution, with deep expertise in at least one enterprise-grade ESP — Braze, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Iterable, , or comparable.

  • You have built complex, event-triggered journeys from scratch: multi-branch logic, wait steps, conditional splits, holdouts, and cross-channel orchestration across email, SMS, push, and in-app.

  • You are fluent in advanced segmentation — behavioral and product-event based, computed attributes, dynamic and personalized content — and you have scaled a program where segmentation drove a real increase in send volume.

  • You have built the funnel that matters here: lead capture forms and opt-in logic, welcome series, first-conversion sequences, and subscription activation journeys.

  • You have implemented loyalty, rewards, and win-back programs, and you treat driving repeat purchase and long-term value as a core outcome rather than a nice-to-have.

  • You own deliverability as a discipline: domain warming and authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI), sending reputation, list hygiene, sunset policies, and what to do when a list grows very fast.

  • You own the channel KPIs — open, click, click-to-open, conversion, deliverability, bounce, spam complaints, unsubscribe — and you can diagnose a drop in any of them.

  • You are comfortable with HTML and CSS for email, and you know how to build templates and modules that render correctly across clients. Liquid, Handlebars, AMPscript, or a similar templating language is a strong plus.

  • You understand data flows into the ESP: API-based events, webhooks, ETL or CDP integrations, and product event streams. You can hold a technical conversation with a client's engineering team.

  • You are a systematic troubleshooter — you isolate variables, you check the data before the theory, and you document what you find.

  • You design and execute proper tests: A/B and multivariate, with honest reads on significance.

  • Excellent written communication and the ability to explain a technical problem to a non-technical audience clearly and without condescension.

A day in the life

  • Build and QA the flows, automations, and campaigns that run your client's program — from lead capture and welcome through activation, loyalty, repeat purchase, and win-back.

  • Implement the segmentation and audience logic behind the calendar, and build the dynamic content that makes personalization work at volume.

  • Own the technical setup and health of the client's ESP instance: integrations, data feeds, event tracking, templates, and modules.

  • Monitor and own channel performance and deliverability, escalating and fixing issues before they affect the program.

  • Troubleshoot anything that misfires — a flow that does not trigger, a segment that under-populates, a template that breaks in Outlook — and document the fix.

  • QA every build end to end before launch: logic, rendering, links, personalization, suppression.

  • Design and run the testing roadmap with your Associate Director, and report results honestly.

  • Partner with the Copy & Content Specialist to get copy and creative into the build accurately and on schedule.

  • Build and maintain the reporting your Associate Director needs for client KPI reviews.

What It's Like to Work at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

  • Compensation: The base salary range for this role is $60,000-$80,000 per year. About Us
OurRitual is a fast-growing digital platform reshaping how relationship therapy works. We call it Continuous Therapy. We've reached product-market fit with strong growth, exceptional engagement, and retention that breaks the category. We're pre-Series A, at the stage where AI moves from feature to foundation — and that shift runs straight through data.
Role Overview
As Data Lead, you will own how data gets turned into decisions across the company — and lead the shift from traditional BI into AI-driven BI, powered by agents that surface insight in real time. You'll work closely with one data engineer today, with room to grow the team as scope expands.
You'll define what the data function looks like when AI is embedded in it, not bolted on — from the underlying infrastructure to the dashboards and agents people actually use. The playbook for AI-native BI is still being written, and you'll write a lot of it.
Key Responsibilities
Data Strategy & Ownership

  • Own the vision and roadmap for the data function, including the shift from classic BI to agent-based, AI-driven BI

  • Set priorities in partnership with senior leadership

  • Work closely with a data engineer today, with the option to grow the team as the function scales

AI-Driven BI & Agents

  • Drive adoption of AI across data workflows — from automating analyses to agents answering business questions in real time

  • Own the semantic and metrics layer so every dashboard and every agent reads the same definitions

  • Build in a git-based workflow: dashboards and queries live in git, edited through PRs, built with agents

  • Expose our data to agents over MCP so business questions get answered without waiting for a dashboard

  • Define where AI speeds things up — and where human judgment still has to hold the line

Infrastructure & Analytics

  • Own the data infrastructure: BigQuery, dbt, pipelines, and data reliability

  • Lead complex analytics work, A/B testing, and impact measurement, hands-on

  • Define evals and quality metrics for AI features and agents — not just A/B tests on dashboards

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner with product, marketing, finance, operations, and engineering to define analytical needs and turn them into solutions

  • Represent the data function to the organization — senior-level storytelling with data

Skills & Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in data roles, spanning both analytics and infrastructure

  • Strong analytical foundation — you understand what makes analysis rigorous, not just what makes it automatable, and can use that to build an AI-driven analytics system that's actually trustworthy

  • Hands-on experience integrating AI into data workflows — building it, not just using it; you've shipped an agent or AI analysis flow that people actually use

  • Strong SQL skills and experience building scalable data infrastructure

  • Track record owning data projects independently with stakeholders across the business

  • Solid grounding in experimentation and statistical methods

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills at a leadership level

  • Comfortable being the most senior (and often only) data voice in the room

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Experience with dbt

  • Experience with Amplitude

  • Experience with BigQuery

  • Experience with git-based BI workflows or tools like Modus

  • B2C environment experience

Why This Role
Data teams are about to look very different — not because dashboards disappear, but because people expect answers faster than a weekly report can deliver. This is a rare opportunity to define what AI-native data leadership looks like at a company sitting on a dataset that doesn't exist anywhere else, with real ownership over how the function grows. If you want to build the data function that a category-defining product deserves, this is it.

jobs.description:
Overview

The HRU requires a remote Occupational Health Physician support to provide case review services of occupational medical exams performed for medical clearance, medical surveillance, reasonable accommodation, medical review board, and other purposes as needed by the DEA. This review is provided by a Reviewing Medical Officer (RMO) who makes a recommendation for clearance based on the medical information provided to make a medical recommendation to the DEA regarding an applicant or employee’s ability to perform their job duties safely.

Location: Remote for the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) located at 75 Morrissette Dr, Springfield, VA 22152

Pay: $140/hr

Schedule: Services shall be provided Monday - Friday between the hours of 0830 - 1700 EST. Averaging 40 hours each week

Position Type: Independent Contractor (1099)

Responsibilities

Perform duties of Reviewing Medical Officer (RMO) to make medical recommendations to DEA about a worker’s ability to perform their job duties safely by reviewing exams and associated medical documents within 30 days of receiving paperwork.

Communicate daily with DEA Health Services Unit staff to determine work priorities, issues encountered, and discuss individual exams as needed. RMO will communicate as needed to 3rd parties such as personal or treating physicians in order to successfully and accurately issue a clearance determination.

Provide weekly reports to the DEA on productivity.

Utilize federal, agency specific, and industry medical standards established prior to the examination to make a medical determination of fitness for duty.

Perform clearance case reviews; make a determination about whether the applicantor employee meets job specific medical standards to safely perform work that is arduous, involve a high degree of sensitivity toward the public or sensitive national security concerns, or put employees at risk of hazardous exposures during the course of performing essential job functions. The RMO determination shall address:

  • Whether the applicant or employee is medically cleared to work with or without
  • Whether the applicant or employee is medically able or unable to work.
  • Employee has a suspected work-related injury or illness.
  • Whether or not additional information is needed to make the medical
  • Whether to accelerate exam frequency and/or further evaluation such as additionalmedical testing or a Fitness for Duty evaluation is warranted.

Case reviews shall include examinations performed prior to employment for applicants, for periodic medical evaluation of incumbents, before return to work after an injury, or to determine an incumbent’s ongoing fitness for duty when a change in health status has caused concern about the worker’s or others’ safety.

When conducting medical screening and medical surveillance case reviews, the RMO determines whether there is a change in the health status of an employee due to apotential exposure at work. Requirements for these examinations fall under the general OSHA standard. The RMO determination will address:

  • Whether the health status of an employee has changed due to a potential workplace exposure.
  • Whether work areas require further evaluation due to medical information that raises suspicion for an unsafe work environment.

In determining medical support for medical employability case review, agency specific requests shall include:

  • Reasonable Accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act
  • Leave under the Family Medical Leave Act
  • Medical Fitness for Duty evaluations
  • Return to work after illness or injury
  • Handicapped parking requests
  • Federal disability retirement applications
  • Advanced sick leave and leave bank requests
  • Hardship requests

The RMO shall provide consultative occupational medical services related to agency and occupational health needs. The consultative services may include:

  • Subject Matter Expertise in Medical Review Board proceedings
  • Assistance with developing medical guidelines and standards
  • Creating agency policies and standard operating procedures for medical issues
  • Providing medical guidance on and evaluations for specific occupational medicine issues that arise in the workplace

In any instance, absence of specific guidance for medical determinations requires RMO research and expertise in collaboration with agency POC to develop consistent protocols for evaluation.

Transmission: Encrypted documents will be furnished electronically to RMO’s DEA email address, and will be returned via same. All communications should be via DEA email or shared folder.

The Contractor’s management organization shall be responsible for ensuring that all work activities are performed in a timely and cost-effective manner while maintaining the highest quality of performance. The Contractor shall: (1) prepare monthly status reports; and (2) participate in ad hoc status meetings. The Contractor shall ensure that project management activities are reflective of all active task orders.

Litigation Support. The Contractor’s reviewing physicians, specialists, or other staff may berequired to provide legal testimony or testify in court proceedings for the DEA. These services may include:

    • Providing copies of medical files and related documentation
    • Ad hoc consulting
    • Participate in investigatory interviews in person or by electronic means
    • Prepare affidavits
    • Participate in depositions by electronic means
    • Provide testimony by electronic means

Qualifications

  • Experience: Minimum 12 months specialized expertise and experience rendering opinions about whether an applicant or employee is medically qualified to perform the duties of their position, with or without accommodation.
  • Education: Completed Undergraduate Program and Medical School (MD/DO).Specialized training in Occupational Health Medicine.
  • Licensure: Unrestricted state licensure in state of practice
  • Certification: General Practitioner, at minimum; Contractor shall be a board-certified in Occupational Health Medicine or board-certified in Preventive Medicine
  • Malpractice Insurance: Provider is required to provide their own malpractice insurance.
  • Demonstrate the ability to convey expert medical opinions and advice using excellent communication skills. Communications will primarily be in writing. If needed, contractor shall be able to provide expert witness testimony related to case reviews performed.

The qualified candidate would assist with audit preparation, evidence collection, compliance tracking, and status reporting, ensuring that the required materials are accurate, up to date, and delivered on time. This is a part-time position (25 hours per week), with the potential to transition to a full-time role.

DUTIES OF THE POSITION:

Compliance & Audit Support

  • Support ISO, SOC 2, and CMMC compliance activities under the direction of the Director of Compliance
  • Assist with internal and external audit preparation, including:
  • Collecting requested evidence
  • Tracking auditor requests
  • Organizing documentation for review
  • Maintain compliance artifacts such as control matrices, evidence folders, spreadsheets, and trackers
  • Track remediation items and follow up with control owners as directed

Documentation & Administration

  • Update and maintain compliance documentation, policies, procedures, and logs as instructed
  • Manage version control and ensure documentation is current and properly stored
  • Prepare draft reports, summaries, and status updates for compliance leadership
  • Maintain audit calendars, timelines, and task lists

Coordination & Communication

  • Coordinate meetings related to compliance and audits, including scheduling, agendas, notes, and action-item tracking
  • Serve as a point of contact for routine compliance-related requests and information gathering
  • Communicate clearly with internal teams to obtain documentation and updates, escalating issues when needed

Program Support

  • Assist with maintaining awareness of compliance requirements across applicable frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2, CMMC)
  • Support compliance training and awareness activities as directed
  • Perform other compliance-related administrative or support tasks as assigned

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 1 – 3 years of experience in a compliance support, audit support, risk, security, IT administration, or similar operational role
  • Experience supporting audits, compliance programs, or regulated environments is preferred
  • Ability to follow established processes and execute tasks accurately and on time
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills
  • High attention to detail, especially when handling documentation and evidence
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously
  • Strong, clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Familiarity with information security or compliance concepts
  • Exposure to one or more frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST, or CMMC is a plus
  • Basic understanding of data protection and secure handling of information
  • Ability to take direction and execute tasks independently once assigned
  • Comfortable working with sensitive and confidential information
  • Reliable, methodical, and process-oriented
  • Willingness to learn and grow within a compliance function

THE FOLLOWING SKILLS ARE PREFERRED BUT NOT REQUIRED:
  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Business, or a related field
  • Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered

Communitas is a church planting organization with 50 years experience working in Western Europe, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America and North America. Our leading edge ministry is looking for the right person to help lead us into greater Kingdom ministry. Our current mission family of over 200 includes full-time, bi-vocational employees, as well as affiliates, with many of that number being non-Americans. Communitas operates in over 20 different countries as we start new initiatives and nurture churches and church-planting projects toward reproducible maturity.

Communitas is rooted in missional theology. Our three core values center on being Kingdom seeking, Grace oriented and People focused. Our church planting methodology is not tied to a specific formula, but rather the spirit of serving others and the embracing of a progression of actions that lead to a healthy, maturing church, making our approach very adaptable to unique contexts (see for details). We are pioneers and risk takers. We value honesty and encouragement. We collaborate well, within our global regions, as well as with partner organizations.

The Need and Opportunity

Across post-Christian secular culture people have largely given up on church, but spirituality remains important to them. Communitas International is at the forefront of sparking that spirituality with mission and helping people ‘taste and see that the Lord is good’. Our church planting organization offers the following:

  • A firm commitment to expressing the passionate love of God for the world in word and deed.
  • Substantial experience in reaching people in post-Christian culture.
  • Strategic coaching for planters and churches by experienced cross-cultural practitioners.
  • Robust training for team leaders and members via online cohorts, on-site events and regional/global seminars and conferences.
  • Rigorous assessment experiences and tools that can form the basis for strategic coaching and healthy team building.
  • Partnership in innovation with those looking for new ways to declare the timeless message of the Gospel.

Regional Advancement Director

Local and/or cross-cultural clergy and lay ministry leaders

Location:

Typically outside USA

Exempt

Yes, upon commissioning or ordination

The role is responsible for establishing and cultivating a missionally focused community of faith, guiding its growth from initial launch through long-term sustainability.

The planting pastor will utilize the proven methodology of the Communitas network of churches—embedding, initiating, practicing, maturing, hubbing, and extending—to shape the church’s formation, rhythms, and community life. This framework provides a foundation for healthy church development while allowing flexibility to adapt to the unique cultural context, needs, and opportunities of the local community.

The specific scope of responsibilities will vary according to the location, stage of church development, and ministry needs of the area served. The role requires both strategic leadership and contextual adaptability to foster a thriving, multiplying community of faith.

  • Demonstrates professionalism, discretion, and integrity in all matters.
  • Maintains a collaborative, learning-oriented, and positive leadership posture.
  • Commits to excellence in communication, stewardship, and organizational representation.

About Us

No Isolation is an award-winning scale-up in EdTech on a global mission to help education providers ensure learning and belonging for all children. With offices in Oslo, London, and Munich, we provide the technology and solutions required to tackle the societal challenge of school absence, empowering institutions to uphold academic continuity and inclusion for every student.

Our flagship solution, the AV1 robot, is deployed across 19 countries with 5,000+ units, supporting schools to sustain attendance, belonging, and continuity of learning for children who cannot be physically present. Consistently described as life-changing, it bridges the gap between the student and their peers, restoring both educational continuity and the essential sense of social belonging.

The Opportunity

We are already quite established in Germany. With 1,500+ units already deployed nationwide, it’s a proven, trusted, and loved solution - used by teachers who need a reliable way to include absent students, welcomed by families who feel their child is still “there,” and embraced by pupils who can see, speak, and belong again. The references are real, and the impact is repeatable at scale.

Our next chapter is expanding our footprint in North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW) - a strategic, organic expansion that extends what already works. As Germany's most populous state, NRW represents a massive and vital opportunity for our mission. We’re bringing the same quality, reliability, and outcomes that defined success elsewhere, and we’re looking for a senior enterprise sales professional to play a pivotal role in driving growth across this vast region.

As Account Manager, you will set your strategic focus, open executive-level doors across education and city authorities, and orchestrate multi-stakeholder decisions. Your craft is relationships: You’ll cultivate a high-trust network across all your stakeholders - engaging in person to move complex decisions forward. You will lead with rigor, listen with empathy, and with executive credibility, you’ll turn early wins into lighthouse references, and lay the operating cadence that keeps momentum compounding year after year.

What You’ll Do

  • Define and drive your territory strategy: Build and execute the go-to-market plan for your focus area within the region - segmentation, territory mapping, prioritizing key accounts, and setting milestones that turn strategic goals into tangible outcomes

  • Build strategic executive relationships: Build trust with education authorities, municipal leaders, and school executives - map decision paths, align to policy and budget cycles, and secure multi-level sponsorship

  • Win and expand strategic accounts: Lead full-cycle acquisition and growth; align executive sponsors, budget owners, and procurement; run multi-stakeholder close plans to signed agreements

  • Lead with consultative, framework-led sales: Combine solution selling with proven methodologies (e.g., MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, SPIN, Challenger) to pressure-test value, control timelines, and move from business case to signed terms

  • Collaborate for seamless delivery and growth: Partner with Customer Success, Marketing, and Product teams to ensure smooth onboarding and implementation, capture outcomes, and turn success into expansion and credible references

  • Create regional momentum: Build a trusted partner network (associations, advocacy groups, integrators) to accelerate adoption, and build visible presence by speaking at and hosting conferences, roundtables, and policy forums to shape the inclusion agenda

What You Bring

  • Enterprise new-business track record (Germany): Extensive B2B enterprise experience - creating and closing multi-stakeholder deals, managing long cycles, and driving consensus to close

  • Executive relationship builder: Ability to build credibility and earn trust from C-suite to school leaders - advancing complex decisions through purposeful face-to-face engagement and secure executive sponsorship

  • Strategic GTM & execution discipline: Ability to build a targeted GTM strategy and turn it into an operating rhythm - market segmentation, decision-maker mapping, phased milestones, pipeline hygiene, and accurate forecasting (HubSpot)

  • Structured, consultative selling: Ability to run structured discovery and build quantified ROI cases; experience with methodologies such as MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, SPIN or Challenger is beneficial

  • Language & location: Native-level German and professional English; based anywhere within the NRW region

What We Offer

  • Attractive uncapped OTE model: Base salary, performance bonus, and uncapped commission

  • Proven platform to build on: Expand within NRW with national credibility - strong references, delivery know-how, and clear demand signals

  • Territory ownership & autonomy: Take ownership of a key territory within Germany's largest market, where you will work with strong autonomy and decision space

  • Growth & development: Meaningful opportunities to learn (enablement, coaching, industry events) and shape best practice as we expand in Germany

  • Tools, enablement & cross-functional support: Dedicated partnership with Customer Success, Marketing, and Product; collateral, case studies, and training to win and scale

  • A purpose-led culture: An environment that sets high standards and gives you the space to do your best work

Location

This is a remoteposition that can be based anywhere within North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW). You should be happy to travel regularly across the NRW region, particularly for heavy outbound sales activities with local municipalities.

You will report to our Head of Sales in Germany and collaborate closely with teams in Munich, London, and Oslo. While the role is remote, our Munich office offers the chance to connect and collaborate in person when desired.

About bunny.net

Some people accept the internet as it is. We see what it could be.

At bunny.net, we don’t wait for change. We make it happen. You won’t find layers of red tape or play-it-safe thinking here. You’ll find people who move quickly, take ownership, and push ideas all the way to the edge. Literally.

You’ll build things that solve actual problems, not add to them.

We’re not perfect, and we don’t pretend to be. But we’re always improving. We’re looking for people who want to do the same, who take pride in their work, and aren’t afraid to challenge what’s possible.

Because everyone deserves a better internet. And we’re here to help it hop faster.

UX Lead

The internet runs on infrastructure. But using that infrastructure shouldn't feel... well, like infrastructure.

That's where you come in.

As our UX Lead, you'll help shape how developers experience bunny.net.

Working closely with product managers and engineers, you'll own the UX journey from early product ideas through to polished experiences developers love using.

This isn't a role where you'll approve every mockup. You'll be hands-on where it matters most, solving meaningful product challenges while building the systems, patterns, and culture that help great UX scale across bunny.net.

You'll spend your time experimenting with new ideas, using AI to move faster, and continuously refining the experiences we build.

The best UX often goes unnoticed, because everything just works.

If that excites you, you'll feel right at home.

  • Make powerful technology feel beautifully simple

  • Shape the experience of products used by developers around the world

  • Work side by side with product managers and engineers to solve tough problems

  • Build the systems and design patterns that help great UX scale

  • Clear communication and the confidence to explain your thinking to anyone, from engineers to leadership

Europe, ideally within CET ±3 hours so collaboration with the team feels natural rather than scheduled.

jobs.excerpt: Principal Product Manager – ISV & IntegrationsContext & Impact: Lansweeper's Product Management team is growing, and we're looking for a Principal Product Manager to take strategic ownership of our ISV and integrations domain.
jobs.description:
Principal Product Manager – ISV & Integrations

Context & Impact:
Lansweeper's Product Management team is growing, and we're looking for a Principal Product Manager to take strategic ownership of our ISV and integrations domain. This isn't a role that sits above the work — it's one that drives it. You'll shape how Lansweeper embeds its capabilities into partner ecosystems, defines integration strategy across domains, and sets the standard other Product Managers measure themselves against.

Over the next six to twelve months, success means the ISV and integrations domain has a clear, defensible strategy, active partner relationships that are moving forward, and a growing footprint of embedded capabilities across the ecosystem.

Challenge:

The main challenges you'll face are:

  • Earning trust across a complex partner ecosystem. ISV and integration work means navigating relationships with resellers, MSPs, and independent software vendors — each with their own priorities. Building the credibility to drive alignment across those relationships, while also managing internal stakeholders, takes a PM who has genuinely done this before.

  • Operating across domains without losing depth. As a Principal PM, you won't just own one domain — you'll influence strategy across the broader product organisation. Staying sharp on ISV and integrations while contributing credibly at initiative level requires both breadth and discipline.

  • Holding the bar in a high-performing team. Lansweeper's Product organisation is mature and the expectations are genuinely high. You won't just need to hold your own — you'll be the standard others measure themselves against.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Shape initiative-level strategy across domains as a genuine thought partner to the Product Leadership Team, with a primary focus on ISV partnerships and integrations

  • Research and build the business case for company-level bets, including opportunities to embed Lansweeper's capabilities into partner platforms and ecosystems

  • Define what good discovery and validation look like across the organisation — set the standard, don't just follow it

  • Engage prospects, customers, and partners at the most senior level to validate roadmap direction, including ISV partners, resellers, and MSPs

  • Collaborate with UX and Engineering through the full product lifecycle — from requirements and prototypes through to delivery — and step into any domain's delivery problem when it matters most

  • Build and evolve Lansweeper's partner ecosystem, including ISV relationships, integration partners, resellers, and MSPs

  • Drive go-to-market activities including release communications and enablement, in close partnership with Product Marketing

  • Shape how the Product organisation works — contribute to standards, practices, and the hiring bar

Key Requirements:

Hard skills:

  • 10+ years of hands-on Product Management experience in B2B SaaS — this is a hard floor, not a guideline

  • Proven track record of owning complex, data-driven products end to end, including coordinating delivery across multiple concurrent workstreams

  • Direct experience working with ISV partners, integration ecosystems, or embedded product capabilities — managing integrations, embedding features into partner platforms, or building out a partner channel is highly relevant

  • Strong market research skills and experience building business cases for company-level product bets

  • Fluency across multiple communication formats — live presentations, written specs, partner briefings, webinars, and more

  • Experience engaging mid-market and enterprise stakeholders at every level of seniority, including resellers, MSPs, and integration partners

  • Familiarity with system and device management, network infrastructure, or adjacent domains is a plus — not a requirement

Soft skills:

  • Resilient and adaptable — you absorb reprioritisation without losing your footing, and you bring your team along with you

  • Collaborative by default — you pull people together across functions and understand that driving something from start to finish means more than staying in your lane

  • Self-driven — you identify what's next, build the case, and move; you don't wait to be told

AI Specific Skills:
Lansweeper is an AI-native company and we need people aligned with that strategy. People who are genuinely curious about AI and have a proven trackrecord in empowering their workflows with AI agents.

Team Info:
You'll join Lansweeper's Product Management team — a mature, high-performing group working across distinct product domains. Cross-functional collaboration is central to how you'll operate, working closely day-to-day with Engineering, UX, and Product Marketing from discovery through to go-to-market. As a Principal PM, you'll also contribute beyond your own domain, helping to raise the bar across the broader product organisation.

Our Offer:
Our offer is country-specific and will be discussed with you according to what’s relevant in your case before our first call.

About Lansweeper:
Lansweeper is the AI Cyber Asset Intelligence platform helping IT and Security teams gain full visibility, reduce cyber risk, and scale automation with confidence.

In today's complex IT, OT, cloud, and IoT environments, fragmented asset data slows decisions and increases risk. We transform raw asset data into a continuously validated, trusted source of truth — so teams can move faster and act with certainty.

With Lansweeper, organisations can:

See – Truly complete visibility across hybrid environments
Know – Enriched asset intelligence with lifecycle and risk context
Act – Automate workflows, coordinate remediation, and enforce policy at scale

From universal asset discovery to AI-powered intelligence, we provide the shared foundation modern IT Operations, Cybersecurity, and Digital Transformation teams rely on.

Our culture:

We're built on four core values:

  • One Team – United across boundaries

  • We Care – Customers and people at the center

  • We Grow – Learning, sharing, improving

  • We Deliver – Focusing on what truly matters

Pay Transparency:
At Lansweeper, every role is assigned to a level defined by three things: the expertise it requires, the complexity it involves, and the scope of impact it carries.
Each level maps to a salary band based on salary benchmarks from the Software/SaaS industry of your country, so your pay reflects what the market pays for comparable roles.
The gross salary range for this role depends on the country where the candidate will be hired — discuss salary expectations with the recruiter.
Where you land within that range depends on the expertise you bring, the complexity you have navigated, the scope of impact you have owned, and your track record of delivering results in comparable roles — the same criteria applied consistently to every candidate.
We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, religion, ethnic origin, age, sexual orientation, or disability.

jobs.excerpt: About Command|Link Command|Link is a global SaaS Platform providing network, voice services, and IT security solutions, helping corporations consolidate their core infrastructure into a single vendor and layering on a proprietary single pane of glass platform.
jobs.description:
About Command|Link

Command|Link is a global SaaS Platform providing network, voice services, and IT security solutions, helping corporations consolidate their core infrastructure into a single vendor and layering on a proprietary single pane of glass platform. Command|Link has revolutionized the IT industry by tackling the problems our competitors create. In recognition for our unprecedented innovation and dedication, Command|Link was recognized as the SD-WAN Product of the Year, ITSM Visionary Spotlight, UCaaS Product of the Year, NaaS Product of the Year, Supplier of the Year, and the AT&T Strategic Growth Partner. Command|Link has built the only IT platform for scale that solves ISP vendor sprawl and IT headaches. We make it easy for our customers to get more done, maximize uptime and improve the bottom line.

Learn more about us here!

This is a 100% remote position

About your new role:

CommandLink's monitoring product is how customers see their network: every device, service, and dependency, surfaced through an API and UI they use every day. Today that experience is harder to build well than it looks, most platforms in this space bury the signal in flat device lists and dated interfaces. We want to build something clearer and faster, grounded in real network topology instead.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll own that surface end to end: the architecture that determines how it scales, how it consumes the classification and telemetry layers beneath it, and how it evolves as the platform grows. This is full-stack work with a strong network domain emphasis. You'll need to reason clearly about both system design and the experience it produces for someone troubleshooting their network in real time.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the architecture and long-term direction of the monitoring product's API and UI, including the roadmap for how it scales and evolves.
  • Surface the full account and device hierarchy, from company down through site, probe and collector, device, and service, along with the dependency relationships between them, in a way that stays navigable at scale.
  • Lead the discovery and inventory experience: how new devices and hosts are found and billed (Host Discovery), how correlated system summaries are built (System Discovery), and how customers onboard new sources.
  • Build the screens customers use to create, edit, and review alert history through the alert service.
  • Define the data contracts between the monitoring product and the classification, telemetry, and alert services it depends on, and hold the line on their quality as the platform grows.
  • Set the technical patterns other engineers follow for rendering and interacting with complex, hierarchical network data, including topology visualizations that are genuinely performant, a known weak point across competing platforms.
  • Dive into other teams' projects when architecture, performance, or design decisions need your judgment, and resolve cross-team dependencies before they become blockers.
  • Mentor engineers across the team and raise the bar for what production-grade, domain-aware full-stack work looks like at CommandLink.
  • Takes on additional responsibilities and projects as needed to support the success of the team and organization.

What you'll need for success:

Required

  • Deep understanding of network and system topology: how devices, services, and infrastructure relate to each other, and how to represent those relationships clearly to someone troubleshooting live.
  • Production experience with high-volume, latency-sensitive infrastructure: distributed messaging/event streaming (e.g. Kafka) and search or indexing at scale (e.g. OpenSearch), or clear equivalents.
  • Comfort with contract-driven development across teams, using schema/interface definitions like protobuf to keep multiple services honest to a shared contract.
  • Working knowledge of how network telemetry looks in production (SNMP, syslog, ICMP, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and the judgment to reason about what a given signal means for a real network environment.
  • Strong cloud and systems experience across at least two of AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • A track record of owning architectural decisions in ambiguous problem spaces and driving them to durable outcomes, including influencing shared contracts or platform boundaries across teams.

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience building monitoring, observability, or network management products with a customer-facing UI.
  • Familiarity with graph data models and how hierarchical or dependency topology is represented and traversed.
  • Experience designing data visualizations for complex, hierarchical, or graph-structured data.
  • Background with platforms like SolarWinds, Zabbix, PRTG, Auvik, or similar. Understanding what they get right and wrong is the useful part, not having built the better version already.

If you don't check every box here but this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. We're more interested in how you think about this space than a perfect skills match.

Why you'll love life at Command|Link

Join us at CommandLink, where you'll have the opportunity to shape the future of business communication. We value the innovative spirit and seek individuals ready to bring their unique vision and expertise to a team that values bold ideas and strategic thinking. Are you ready to make an impact?

  • Room to grow at a high-growth company
  • An environment that celebrates ideas and innovation
  • Your work will have a tangible impact
  • Flexible time off
  • Fun events at cool locations
  • Employee referral bonuses to encourage the addition of great new people to the team

At CommandLink, we’re committed to creating a fair, consistent, and efficient hiring experience. As part of our process, we use AI-assisted tools to help review and analyze applications. These tools support our recruiting team by identifying qualifications and experience that align with the requirements of each role.

AI tools are used only to assist in the evaluation process — they do not make final hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by a member of our recruiting or hiring team before any decisions are made.

About Ting Labs

Ting Labs is the company behind Ting, an electrical fire prevention sensor active in more than 1.3 million homes across North America. A single Ting sensor takes 30 million measurements per second; across the fleet, the result is one of the largest continuous, high-resolution datasets ever assembled on the residential electrical grid.

Ting's sensor fleet provides real-time visibility into hidden electrical fire hazards across more than a million homes. These insights enable our Ting Fire Safety Team to identify hazards early and help prevent devastating electrical fires before they start.

About the Role

We are hiring a Product Manager to scale Ting’s consumer product and services — owning strategy, roadmap, customer support and insights, GTM, and the web and mobile apps themselves.

This role sits at the intersection of product and marketing. It will partner very closely with marketing to deliver an evolving customer experience, with the goal of growing the Ting installed base through both existing and new channels.

What You'll Own

  • The consumer. Be the in-house expert on consumers' needs - what prompted them to request or buy the product, how they use it, and what new problems it can solve for them. Run discovery, build durable feedback loops, and translate insight into the product roadmap.
  • Internal tools. Evolve the tools used by our Fire Safety Team to increase FST effectiveness and throughput resolving customer’s fire hazards.
  • The experience. Elevate the existing web and mobile experiences and support new flows and customer experiences.
  • Product vision and strategy. Set the North Star direction for the Ting Sensor and Services and the strategy to realize the vision in concert with company leadership.
  • Roadmap definition and delivery. Define and ship the roadmap to make progress towards the vision. Partner with design, engineering, marketing and operations to shape the scope of each release. Measure consumer and business impact of product changes after they’re made.
  • Expand distribution channels. Lead product development in support of new distribution channels in concert with Marketing and Sales. These include D2C, new channel partners, and international expansion.
  • Go-to-market. Partner with marketing on positioning, messaging, pricing and packaging. Ensure a smooth experience regardless of acquisition channel
  • Scalable product operations. Elevate the internal roadmapping, prioritization, and release-planning practices for this product line.
  • AI-native operating. Use modern AI tools fluently across research, prototyping, writing, and analysis — at the pace PMs are now expected to work.

What We're Looking For

Consumer product experience

  • 4+ years of consumer / mobile app product management experience.
  • 2+ years distributing products via D2C channels, experience with subscription-based products, knowledge of churn models and LTV calculations.
  • Strong understanding of how consumers interact with device / software combinations such as wearables, smart home technology and telemetry. Knowledge of how to extract qualitative and quantitative consumer insights to inform the product strategy and roadmap.

Ensures CTMS, dashboards and other systems are set up and available for use by the clinical team, including overseeing user acceptance testing (UAT) as needed. Ensures access and audit trail reviews are conducted as required.

• Coordinates initial and ongoing training to the study team regarding protocol specificities, Case Report Form (CRF) completion, dashboards, Sponsor Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), clinical plans and guidelines, data plans and timelines for the study.

• Oversees resourcing allocations for CRAs and Central Monitors, site assignments and study team members' conduct, and identifies risks to delivery or quality.

• Ensures quality of the clinical monitoring, central monitoring and site management deliverables within a project and maintain proper visibility of its progress by the use of approved systems and / or tracking tools.

• Reviews the project oversight dashboards and other clinical trial systems (e.g. Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), Electronic Data Capture (EDC), eDiary, Electronic Patient Reported Outcomes (ePROs), Trial Master File (TMF), IVRS/IWRS, Central Monitoring dashboards), to oversee site and patient activities, study team conduct and to ensure the data has been updated to reflect timely execution of all operational aspects (required visits/calls, duration, and frequency) according to plan.

• Understands the monitoring strategy required for the study and, where required, participates in the development of the study risk assessment plan. Is accountable for their assigned clinical team members' understanding, ongoing compliance and delivery according to the stated monitoring strategy, CMP/SMP, and risk plans.

• Reviews the content and quality of site and central monitoring documentation (site monitoring calls, site visit reports, site letters, central monitoring reports and pertinent correspondence), to ensure they represent site management activities and conduct and that they appropriately convey any risks to protocol/GCP compliance, trial conduct, patient safety or data integrity. Document requested revisions and approvals in CTMS. Ensures these deliverables are provided according to company and/or sponsor specifications, including delivery deadlines.

• Interacts with the client and other functional departments related to clinical monitoring, central monitoring and site management activities and deliverables. Provides status updates on the clinical deliverables and risks to clients, project management and leadership as per departmental or study agreements. Provides solutions for obstacles in protocol execution and site management.

• Demonstrates understanding of other functions' roles in achieving compliance and delivery according to protocol, SOPs, ICH GCP and country regulations This may include data management, study start up, patient recruitment, medical monitoring, pharmacovigilance and Quality Assurance (QA). Supports Inspection Readiness for clinical trial management scope.

Develop and support execution of corrective action plans at site and study level. Supports and completes activities to achieve data cut and lock deadlines.

• May be assigned to larger, more complex trials or may coordinate clinical activities for a team of CTMs across a portfolio of projects

• May coach and mentor CTMs regarding functional clinical delivery, evaluation of project risks, and action implementation.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience

• Demonstrated ability to lead and align teams in the achievement of project milestones

• Demonstrated capability of working in an international environment.

• Demonstrated expertise in site management and monitoring (clinical or central)

• Preferred experience with risk-based monitoring

• Demonstrates understanding of clinical trial management financial principles and budget management

• Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements

• Must demonstrate good computer skills

• Strong conflict resolution skills

• Demonstrated ability to apply problem solving techniques to resolve complex issues and apply a risk management approach to identifying and mitigating potential threats to the successful conduct of a clinical research project.
